post.summary: Normalize an image reference string
post.description: Parses a pull-style image reference and returns its canonical pullable form along with the structured registry, repository, tag, and digest components. When the input omits a registry, docker.io is assumed; when it omits a tag and has no digest, `latest` is assumed. The first path segment is only treated as a registry host when it contains a `.` or `:` or matches one of `localhost`, `localhost.localdomain`, `localbuild`. As a result, an input like `harbor/proj/img` is normalized as `docker.io/harbor/proj/img:latest`, not as the repository `proj/img` on an internal Harbor registry — callers referencing an internal registry must supply a dotted host (e.g. `harbor.internal/proj/img`) or an explicit port (e.g. `harbor:443/proj/img`).

qualifying_status is accepted and ignored, rather than forbidden. It is server-set
and appears on every stored rule set, so forbidding it meant a client could not
re-submit a rule set it had just read - a GET followed by a PATCH of the same
document was a 422, and the caller had to strip the field first. Create, update

ignore unknown fields: a misspelt days_since_eol is still a 422 rather than a
silently dropped field on a rule that deletes things, and any status other than
eol is still refused. The only thing now accepted is the value the server was
going to stamp anyway.

VulnAnnotationSource.description:
Provenance of a VEX annotation (ENTERPRISE-8935), persisted as the single
JSONB ``source`` column and surfaced as a nested object on responses.

``type`` is the kind of source (``external``/``user``); ``name`` is the
specific source — the application's contact organization name for user
annotations, or the vendor/registry for external ones. Set automatically at
ingestion, never client-supplied on create.

``name`` is required and never null: user annotations resolve it from the app's
effective organization name (its own contact org, falling back to the owning
account's NOT NULL ``organization_name``), and failing to resolve it is an error
rather than a null name.

Each source provides ONE assessment which may contain scores for

CvssSeverity.title: CvssSeverity
CvssSeverity.description:
Qualitative severity rating for a CVSS v3.x/v4.0 score, as defined by
the CVSS specification itself.

Deliberately distinct from Severity (this platform's own, Grype-matching
vocabulary): CVSS's own rating scale has no UNKNOWN, and labels the
bottom tier "none" rather than "negligible" - see the official tables at
https://www.first.org/cvss/v3-1/specification-document and
https://www.first.org/cvss/v4-0/specification-document.

v2.0 uses the separate, narrower CvssV2Severity below - its scale has no
NONE or CRITICAL tier, so a v2 score can never legitimately produce
either rating.

CvssSourceCategory.description: High-level category for CVSS assessment sources.

CvssV2Severity.title: CvssV2Severity
CvssV2Severity.description:
Qualitative severity rating for a CVSS v2.0 score.

v2.0's own rating scale (https://www.first.org/cvss/v2/guide) is a
narrower three-tier table than v3.x/v4.0's - no NONE or CRITICAL rating
exists for v2. Kept as a separate enum from CvssSeverity rather than a
restricted subset of it, so the type itself guarantees a v2 score can
never be typed as NONE or CRITICAL.

MatchedVulnerabilityAnnotation.title: MatchedVulnerabilityAnnotation
MatchedVulnerabilityAnnotation.description:
The VEX annotation resolved for a matched (vulnerability, package) pair,
surfaced as a nested object on the app-version vulnerability display surfaces
(the vulnerability list, packages-by-vulnerability, and policy vulnerability
findings). Carries the annotation's ``status`` (the same value as the item's
flat ``vex_status``), its ``uuid``, and its provenance ``source``.

Named distinctly from the v5 ``VulnerabilityAnnotation`` record schema in the
base swagger (the full CRUD annotation entity) to avoid a generated-schema
collision; this is the terse read-only projection on a match, not that record.

no resolved annotation. The ``source.name`` is display-projected (user
annotations resolve to the app's current organization name) via the
ENTERPRISE-8935 ``display_source_name`` chokepoint; see
``build_vulnerability_annotation``.
